title: Merge sort join postcondition
statement: Let $P$ contain the designated sorting, halving, merging, and copying procedures, and suppose the word bound is at least the space bound. Let $d,a,fr,h,n$ be natural numbers, let $r$ be an integer, and let $S_1,S_2$ be integer lists of lengths $h$ and $n-h$, respectively, with $h\le n$ and $1\le n$. Suppose the memory function $\mu$ stores $S_1$ starting at $a$ and $S_2$ starting at $a+h$, with $a+n\le fr$ and $fr+n\le\mathrm{space}$, and suppose $d<\mathrm{depth}$. Then the join procedure, started with frame $(n,a,fr,h,r)$ and memory $\mu$, has an execution of cost at most $56n+34$ ending in a state with memory $\sigma'.\mathrm{mem}$ for which there is a memory function $\mu'$ that agrees with $\mu$ outside the interval starting at $fr$ of length $n$, stores the merge of $S_1$ and $S_2$ starting at $a$, and agrees with $\sigma'.\mathrm{mem}$ outside the interval starting at $a$ of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: The program contains the specified sort, half, merge, and copy procedures at the designated indices
Space is bounded above by the word limit
